lastText: File ClosedThe Ring, Closed After the FactMinor VictorySoviet High Command, 1939–1945End of hostilities: NOVEMBER 1945 (PROJECTED) · filed out of sequence, pages missingImmediate AftermathVictory in Europe arrives around November 1945: later than the historical May 1945, the price of choices that spent time to save men. The army that reaches Berlin has paid for the ground twice over: a war fought closer to the historical pattern of holding rigid lines regardless of the arithmetic, at the cost this campaign keeps returning to. The industrial evacuation was subordinated to front supply in 1941: easing that autumn's crisis at a cost in Urals production capacity that every later year of this campaign quietly pays for. The tank armies waited for the three fronts to close together and entered Prague on May 11, two days later than they did in the real war. The offensive of January 1942 was concentrated on the Western axis, as Zhukov argued, instead of launched on every front at once, and the whole reserve thrown at one place was still not enough there. No branch of this campaign reaches a different destination, only the timing and the price were ever in Soviet hands.One Year LaterVictory arrived behind the historical May 1945, which means Soviet forces are still consolidating a front the historical record had a year's head start settling by this point. Within the year, the governments this front's advance put in place across Eastern Europe are consolidating along lines this campaign
